drhp.business: Indian Emulsifiers Limited manufactures esters, amphoterics, phosphate esters, imidazolines, wax emulsions, SMO and PIBSA emulsifiers and related intermediates, operating from its manufacturing facility at MIDC Lote Parshuram, Ratnagiri, Maharashtra. The Company focuses on customised formulations and contract manufacturing in close partnership with institutional clients, serving the food, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, home care, industrial cleaning, textiles, mining, oilfield, agriculture and paints sectors.

risks.note: Company faces price volatility dependent on crude oil prices; the SWOT notes this is expected to be partly minimized as both input and output prices are impacted, but it remains a disclosed structural exposure.
As exports grow, sudden Rupee depreciation or appreciation is disclosed as having a short-term impact on realization.

risks.note: Company discloses a threat from competition using new technologies from large global multinationals.
Regulatory challenges, government policies and tax procedures are disclosed as capable of impacting margins.

The Australian subsidiary experienced a temporary slowdown from Australian floods (January 2026) and a fuel shortage (March 2026) affecting customer offtake, and the US subsidiary (Polaris) currently lacks local banking facilities, requiring working capital support via extended shipment credit from the parent until a Board-approved capital infusion is completed.

Debtor days rose from approximately 110 to 131 as the Company's customer mix shifted toward larger accounts with longer standard credit cycles, disclosed as part of MD&A financial performance commentary.
risks.risk: Rising debtor days from customer-mix shift

risks.risk: Related-party transaction and promoter shareholding dilution concerns

risks.note: The Company remains partly restricted from selling its food-grade-capable products into the food industry today due to current facility certification constraints, pending completion of new certified food-grade production infrastructure.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Company faces price volatility dependent on crude oil prices; the SWOT notes this is expected to be partly minimized as both input and output prices are impacted, but it remains a disclosed structural exposure.
- As exports grow, sudden Rupee depreciation or appreciation is disclosed as having a short-term impact on realization.
- Company discloses a threat from competition using new technologies from large global multinationals.
- Regulatory challenges, government policies and tax procedures are disclosed as capable of impacting margins.
- The Australian subsidiary experienced a temporary slowdown from Australian floods (January 2026) and a fuel shortage (March 2026) affecting customer offtake, and the US subsidiary (Polaris) currently lacks local banking facilities, requiring working capital support via extended shipment credit from the parent until a Board-approved capital infusion is completed.
- Debtor days rose from approximately 110 to 131 as the Company's customer mix shifted toward larger accounts with longer standard credit cycles, disclosed as part of MD&A financial performance commentary.
- The proposed rights issue and related investment in Chemical Brothers Enterprises Private Limited (a related party via the Managing Director's stake) drew shareholder concerns on pricing, timing and rationale, alongside promoter shareholding dilution from approximately 48% to approximately 32.64% following the first rights issue.
- The Company remains partly restricted from selling its food-grade-capable products into the food industry today due to current facility certification constraints, pending completion of new certified food-grade production infrastructure.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Commission the Greenfield C3 facility, expanding manufacturing and product capabilities.
- Scale the Australian subsidiary (Southern Emulsifiers Solutions Pty Ltd) toward its three-year cumulative revenue target, with two additional targeted customers expected to come online in FY27.
- Build out the US subsidiary (Polaris Specialty Chemicals Inc.), including a Board-approved working capital infusion, to reduce reliance on extended shipment credit from the parent as it scales.
